**Course source:** Day 1 §3.2–§3.6. **Running system:** Order, Product, and User services.

## Apply Eureka to the shop

The course uses a **Eureka Server** that stores instance records and Eureka Clients in Product, Order and User. Each service registers with a logical name; Order asks for the Product instance list rather than embedding one fixed URL.

~~~text
Order ----GET instance list----> Eureka
  |                               ^
  +----HTTP----> Product A         |
                Product B ---registration/renewal---+
~~~

This changes the *location* problem but does not solve timeouts or overload. Order must still make an HTTP call and handle a failed Product instance.

## Basic lifecycle

A provider starts, submits registration metadata, renews its lease periodically and may deregister during orderly shutdown. The registry can evict instances whose lease has expired. Consumers fetch registry information and may cache it for a configured interval.

The course also introduces **self-preservation**: Eureka can avoid aggressive instance eviction when renewal patterns suggest widespread network trouble. That protects against an inaccurate mass removal, but cached records might include unavailable nodes.

## Instance metadata

Logical service ID and network address are not interchangeable. Metadata can help describe deployment zone, instance identity or supported capabilities; never rely on incidental hostnames as business contracts.

## Minimal conceptual pseudocode

~~~text
Product starts -> registry.register("product", host, port)
Order starts   -> registry.lookup("product") -> [4101, 4104]
Order chooses  -> HTTP GET /products/7
~~~

The runnable Node lab implements the final two Product endpoints and a static list, **not** Eureka itself.

## Historical note

This is an explanation of the original course's Eureka setup. Do not copy its dependency versions or configuration without checking compatibility with the current Spring Cloud release train. A registry should not be added automatically when the deployment platform already provides suitable discovery.

## Mathematical Abstraction

Eureka instance membership changes through registration and expiry.

$$
D_{t+1}(s)=(D_t(s)\cup R_t(s))\setminus X_t(s)
$$

$R_t$ is newly registered membership and $X_t$ removed membership. This is an abstract set transition, not Eureka's exact internal algorithm.
